title: VPC install: failure hypotheses matrix + low-touch probes
content:
Purpose:
This document is a compact, easy-to-run troubleshooting matrix and low-touch smoke-probe list for VPC and on-prem installs that fail in early phases (provisioning, bootstrap, runtime start). It's intended for first responders (SEs, SREs, solutions engineers) to quickly narrow root cause and apply minimally invasive fixes or safe rollbacks.

Scope and constraints:
- Covers common failure buckets observed across customer installs 2023–2025 (network/VPC, TF apply/state, certs, storage, container runtime).
- Focus on checks that can be run without rebuilding clusters or taking long escalations.
- Assumes access to the target environment's bastion host or install-control plane and that the operator has sudo and access to the install terraform state backend.
- Not a replacement for full postmortems; use when a fast recovery is needed.

Quick triage flow (1–10 mins):
1) Confirm symptoms: installer error codes, which phase (terraform plan/apply, bootstrap, runtime-register, first-checkin). Copy the last 10 lines of installer log to a private ticket and Slack.
2) Check provisioning status: cloud provider console / VMware tasks for stuck resources. If instances failed to reach RUNNING, stop here and escalate to infra.
3) Isolate network vs. runtime: run the lowest-touch probes below (DNS, ping/traceroute, control-plane curl). If probes show CSP-level networking blocked, open a networking escalation.
4) If network OK, run TF and runtime sanity checks (state lock, provider version mismatch, disk mounts, containerd start).

Low-touch probes (order matters):
- Control-plane health endpoint (HTTP): curl -sS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:6200/health | head -n1  # adjust port to local agent port
- DNS resolution check: dig +short registry.redwood-inference.internal || host registry.redwood-inference.internal
- IP path to upstream services: traceroute -n 8.8.8.8 (or traceroute -n <gateway>)
- MTU sanity: ping -M do -s 1420 <peer> -c 2  # detect PMTU blackhole
- Throughput smoke: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}s %{size_download}b' http://<artifact-storage>/smallfile.bin
- Port openness: nc -zv <host> <port> (e.g., 22, 2379, 6443, 9200)
- Time skew check: date -u; sudo chronyc sources or timedatectl status
- Disk available & IOPS trap: df -h; iostat -x 1 3 (if iostat available)
- Container runtime: sudo systemctl status containerd || sudo systemctl status docker
- Kernel dmesg tails: sudo dmesg | tail -n 40

Failure hypothesis matrix (short):
- Network restricted by SG/ACLs: symmetry: specific ports failing, traceroute stops, curl to control-plane timed out. Probe: port scan + traceroute. Remediation: open ports per installer docs; check VPC route tables and NAT gateways; confirm IGW/NAT config for egress. Escalation: network team.

- MTU/PMTU blackhole: symptoms: TCP stalls, large payloads fail, small pings OK. Probe: ping with DF bit sizes. Remediation: set MTU on host or overlay to 1400; update CNI config to match.

- DNS resolution inconsistent: symptoms: intermittent name failures, hosts resolve sometimes. Probe: dig +short from each node and from local control-plane. Remediation: use cloud DNS private zones or ensure /etc/resolv.conf points to correct resolver; disable stub resolvers if interfering.

- Terraform state lock/stale lock: symptoms: terraform apply hangs early with state lock message. Probe: check remote state bucket/lock key via terraform backend or cloud console. Remediation: force-unlock after confirming no concurrent run; check backend permission scope.

- Provider/API version mismatch (TF or cloud SDK): symptoms: unknown resource type errors, API 400/422 from provider. Probe: check provider versions in the plan; run terraform providers lock -check. Remediation: pin provider versions used in modules and re-run plan.

- Insufficient instance quotas or flavor mismatch: symptoms: API returns quota-exceeded, or VMs stuck provisioning. Probe: list quotas via API/console. Remediation: ask customer to increase quota or change instance profile.

- Disk/Filesystem mount failures (NVMe/ephemeral): symptoms: pods crash with ENOSPC, kubelet complaining about mount. Probe: lsblk, mount | grep ephemeral, journalctl -u kubelet -n 200. Remediation: ensure disks are attached, format+mount with correct fstype, check udev rules.

- Certificates / time skew: symptoms: TLS handshake failures, x509: certificate signed by unknown authority. Probe: openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -servername <host> | sed -n '1,120p'; date comparisons. Remediation: rotate certs, ensure CA bundles are installed, sync clocks.

- Container runtime OOM/start failures: symptoms: containerd/dockerd repeatedly restarting. Probe: sudo systemctl status containerd -l; journalctl -u containerd -n 200; crictl ps -a. Remediation: free memory, ensure swap/hugepages settings match our preflight, adjust containerd config.

- License/entitlement API blocked: symptoms: bootstrap can't reach licensing endpoint; install stalls in finalize. Probe: curl -v to entitlement endpoint; check proxy settings. Remediation: allow egress or provide offline token.

Observation and log locations (common):
- Installer logs (control host): /var/log/redwood-installer/installer.log
- Terraform logs: ~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache/ and the remote state bucket's audit logs
- Agent logs on nodes: /var/log/redwood-agent/agent.log or systemd journal (journalctl -u redwood-agent)
- Kubelet: /var/log/kubelet.log or journalctl -u kubelet
- Container runtime: /var/log/containers/ and journalctl -u containerd
- Kernel: /var/log/kern.log or dmesg

Quick remediation snippets (copy-paste):
- Reveal state locks: aws s3api get-object --bucket <state-bucket> --key <path>/terraform.tfstate.lock && # or use backend-specific API
- Force-unlock (terraform): terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID> || # ensure no concurrent apply
- Restart agent safely: sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -f -n 200
- Temporary MTU change (quick): sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400 && sudo systemctl restart cni-daemon || # adjust per node

Terraform module notes & gotchas (observed):
- State drift from manual edits: customers frequently hand-edit TF vars when trying to patch a resource; this causes drift that shows up only on apply. Always run terraform plan with -refresh and check diffs.
- Provider upgrades: minor provider upgrades introduced API contract changes in 2024; pin versions in module root and add CHANGELOG notes during upgrades.
- Remote backend permissions: the installer requires read/write/list/object-lock permissions. If backend uses locking (DynamoDB/GCS/Blob), ensure the lock table/bucket exists and is writable.
- Intermittent 409 during apply: usually caused by parallel runs or automation polling; ensure CI/automation respects lock semantics.

Upgrade plan (minimal-impact, preflight + canary):
1) Preflight (run locally against remote state): terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -refresh && run preflight probes listed above. Capture baseline metrics (latency, node CPU/mem, disk utilization).
2) Canary (single AZ or 1 node): apply upgrade to a single node/pool; run smoke probes and run a small synthetic workload for 30–60 mins.
3) Monitor: use agent traces and per-route latency histograms; detect 3x increase in p50/p95 or >1% error rate on control-plane endpoints.
4) Rollback triggers: failed canary checks, persistent OOMs, state corruption during module apply. Have an explicit terraform rollback plan and snapshot volumes where possible.
5) Communication: post a brief incident note in #private-deploys and tag support contacts; keep customer updated every 15 minutes during canary if degraded.

Fingerprint list (short):
- Slow bootstrap with repeated 504/timeout to artifact storage -> check S3/COS presigned URL egress and S3 policy; often NAT egress blocked.
- Terraform plan shows deleted->recreate for IP addresses -> usually CIDR range misalignment between module vars and VPC.
- Repeated kubelet crashloop after upgrade -> check cri runtime version mismatch and kernel module changes (e.g., NVMe updates).

When to escalate (quick guide):
- Anything that requires infra account change (quota increase, route table edits) -> cloud/network team immediately.
- State corruption or partial apply that leaves control-plane half-installed -> engineering-private-deployments + oncall.
- Data loss suspicion (disk reformat, missing PVs) -> pause actions and escalate to SRE + customer data owner.

Notes and unanswered questions (to capture in ticket):
- Did customer run any pre-hooks that mutate VPC or route tables?
- Has the environment been used for other clusters? Are there name collisions on private DNS zones?
- Are there local firewall rules (OS-level) applied by customer automation tools?

Appendix: quick checklist for field SEs (copy into ticket):
- [ ] Confirm installer phase and capture last 50 lines of installer.log
- [ ] Run control-plane curl, dig, traceroute from installer host
- [ ] Check terraform backend lock and provider versions
- [ ] Validate disk mounts and container runtime status on at least 2 nodes
- [ ] Verify time sync and certificate expiry dates
- [ ] If canary/upgrade: snapshot volumes before apply and run canary for >= 30 minutes

If this doc helped, add a short note to GH PR redwood/private-installer#412 or add a bullet to CONFLUENCE: private-deploy-runbooks so we can fold the probe into the formal runbook.
